title: Staged Hydration Agent and Compatibility Checker for Private Upgrades
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Private (VPC/on-prem) customers require upgrades that modify both control plane components and stateful schemas. Existing upgrade flows either perform full cutovers (high risk for large catalogs) or attempt bulk migrations that blow past customer maintenance windows. We need a safer, incremental upgrade assistant that can: apply data/schema changes in small, verified batches; validate binary/runtime compatibility across LTS channels and pinned model versions; create safe rollback points; and expose rollout gates to operator consoles.

Goal: Build a Staged Hydration Agent that orchestrates small, idempotent migration steps (hydrations) with an integrated Compatibility Checker that runs a targeted compatibility matrix (schema, API, runtime kernels, KV cache snapshots). The agent will provide: staged execution, preflight dry-run, divergence detection, automatic pause-on-anomaly, and rollback-safepoints. It should integrate with existing rollout gate primitives (canaries, percentage rollouts, region-based gating) and expose telemetry to the Console and runtime-telemetry dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Agent can execute a sequence of staged hydration steps defined in a migration manifest and mark step-level success/failure
Compatibility Checker runs preflight against a configurable matrix (OS/kernel, runtime-1.xx versions, quantization profile) and reports pass/fail with diffs
Upgrade controller can pause rollout automatically on a compatibility failure or threshold of key metrics (error rate, tail latency, token cost variance)
Rollback safepoints are created as atomic snapshots before destructive steps and restore completes within documented SLA in test clusters
End-to-end dry-run mode produces an artifacts bundle (SQL diffs, resource diffs, KV cache deltas) stored to the upgrade artifacts bucket
design_decisions: Migration manifest DSL: declarative list of hydration steps with idempotency keys and pre/post-check hooks
Idempotency guarantees: each hydration step records a monotonic ledger entry to avoid double-apply across retries
Compatibility Checker: hybrid approach running fast stateless validators locally and fuller integration tests against ephemeral canary nodes
Rollback strategy: transaction-safe snapshots when supported, otherwise compensating steps recorded in manifest
Operator surface: expose detailed step logs and a single-switch pause/resume in Console; gate decisions can be automated or manual
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): prototype hydration step runner + manifest parser; unit-tests for idempotency (2 weeks)
Phase 2: implement Compatibility Checker harness and integrate with CI to run staged-matrix on PRs (3 weeks)
Phase 3: wire agent into private upgrade controller with pause/resume and safepoint creation (3 weeks)
Phase 4: e2e testing on staging clusters with real dataset snapshots and timed rollback drills (2 weeks)
Phase 5: docs, playbook, and Console integration (1 week)
Deliverables: manifest spec, agent binary, compatibility test matrix, dashboard panels, runbook
telemetry_and_alerting: Per-step duration histogram and 99th percentile time
Number of retries and idempotency conflicts metric
Compatibility check pass/fail counts and diff artifact links
Automatic PagerDuty policy when rollout is paused for >10 minutes by automated gate
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest parsing and idempotency ledger
Integration tests: run staged hydration on a copy of customer schema and verify end-state invariants
Chaos test: injector that kills nodes mid-step to verify roll-forward and rollback behavior
Performance test: ensure safepoint snapshot/restore meets SLA for medium and large cluster sizes
Compatibility regression: add matrix entries to CI and verify PR gating
security_and_compliance_notes: Migration artifacts containing customer data must be encrypted at rest using KMS keys (follow Private deployment KMS patterns)
Agent must respect RBAC: only members with upgrade role can trigger non-dry-run flows
Compatibility Checker must not exfiltrate customer data in artifact diffs; scrubbing rules applied to artifacts
risks: Data-sensitive diffs leaking in artifact bundles if scrubbing misses patterns
Long-running hydration steps could exceed customer maintenance windows for very large datasets
Underestimated edge-case in idempotency leading to state divergence across nodes
Compatibility matrix combinatorics may blow up; need to prioritize high-risk axes
rollout_plan: Internal alpha: run on internal staging clusters with synthetic data (week 0)
Beta: opt-in for 3 non-production customer sandboxes behind feature flag (week 1-2)
Canary: gated 5% of private clusters with detailed telemetry and human-on-call monitoring (week 3)
Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with automated gating thresholds and rollback drills at each step
notes: Spike results: prototype hydration runner completed and demonstrates idempotency via ledger entries (see PR #412)
We will reuse the existing safepoint snapshot API from ENG-173501 to avoid re-implementing snapshots
Ask: infra to allocate two staging clusters for e2e tests and two large clusters for perf/rollback
